chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Be endowed with good character, for indeed good character is undoubtedly Paradise, and beware of bad character, for indeed bad character is undoubtedly Hell.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of good and bad character in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith underscores the centrality of *husn al-khuluq* (excellence of character) as a definitive criterion for entry into Paradise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on moral refinement as an extension of prophetic sunnah. The binary contrast between good and bad character serves as a practical ethical guide, linking internal spiritual states directly to eternal destiny, a theme frequently elaborated upon by the Ahl al-Bayt in their teachings on *adab* and *akhlaq*.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-41 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “I advise you to be good-tempered as undoubtedly a good-tempered person will go to Paradise. I admonish you against being bad-tempered, since a bad-tempered person will undoubtedly go to Hell.”
